# Replication comparison — Bai, Jia & Yang (2023, QJE) “Web of Power”

*Generated by `Program/statspai/make_comparison.py`.*  
**Paper values** = the authors' own outputs shipped in the package (`Results/author_outputs/*.txt`, produced 13 Oct 2022 by `All_in_One.do`), cross-checked against the tables of NBER WP 28667 (revised Aug 2022 = the accepted version; the QJE PDF itself is paywalled). Where the WP table differs from the author output the WP number is used and flagged.  
**Original Stata** = our rerun of the package in Stata 18 MP (`Program/run_original.do`, `Results/Tables/*.txt`).  **StatsPAI** = `Program/statspai/replicate_tables.py` / `replicate_figures.py` (StatsPAI 1.28.0, Python 3.13).  
Status: ✅ identical at reported precision (3 decimals, N) · ⚠️ small difference, explained · ❌ failure.

Figure numbering follows the package / NBER WP (Figure 3 … 8). In the published QJE article the same figures are numbered one higher (Figure IV … IX), as also noted by the I4R comment (Buchot et al. 2024).

## 4. StatsPAI `hdfe_ols` issue record

| regression | var | Stata b (se) | sp.hdfe_ols b (se) | iters | dof_fe | sp.feols + reghdfe dof b (se) |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Table 2 col 1 (FE year+county) | `Zeng_all0_invdist_Post` | 0.21356 (0.05809) | 0.21356 (0.05809) | 2 | 89 | 0.21356 (0.05809) |
| Table 4 col 1 (FE year+county+pref x year) | `invdist0_L1_Post` | -0.02769 (0.25351) | -0.02768 (0.25557) | 2 | 296 | -0.02768 (0.25351) |
| Table 4 col 9 Huai (FE year+county+pref x year) | `invdist0_L1_Post` | 0.02139 (0.04742) | 0.01965 (0.04502) | 2 | 506 | 0.02139 (0.04742) |
| Table 4 col 11 Huai | `invdist0_F1_Post` |  () | -0.11995 (0.10175) | 2 | 506 | -0.11545 (0.10634) |

With `year` nested in `prefidXyear`, `sp.hdfe_ols` over-counts absorbed dof by 14 (SEs ≈0.8% too large). In the Huai columns it also keeps two controls (`lncntypop_Post`, `lncntyarea_Post`) that are collinear with prefecture×year FEs up to float32 noise — Stata/pyfixest omit them — giving coefficients of ±4.8e5 and moving the coefficient of interest by 8%. Therefore all one-way-clustered regressions use `sp.feols` (pyfixest backend) + reghdfe's dof formula.
